questions.qtext:
Below are presented two formal languages over the alphabet $\{a, b, c\}$ :
$$
\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{L}_{1}=\left\{a^{n} b^{n} \mid n>1\right\} \\\\
& \mathrm{L}_{2}=\left\{b^{n} a^{p} c^{q} \mid n \geq 0, p \geq 0, q \geq 0\right\}
\end{aligned}
$$
Consider the following statements:

  1. $\mathrm{L}_{1}$ is a regular language.
     
  2. $\mathrm{L}_{2}$ is a regular language.
     
  3. $\mathrm{L}_{2}$ is a context-free language.


Which statements are correct?

questions.qtext: Mark the INCORRECT statement.

options.text: There exists a Turing machine $\text{U}$ that simulates any other Turing machine $\text{M}$ on any input to $\text{M}$.
Church's Thesis states that the informal concept of effective procedure is captured by the formal concept of a Turing machine.
A language is recursively enumerable if, and only if, it is accepted by some Turing machine.

There exists a Turing machine $\text{T}$ such that, given any Turing machine $\text{M}$ and any input $\text{w}$ for $\text{M}$ , $\text{T}$ determines, in a finite number of steps, whether $\text{M}$ halts for the input $\text{w}$ or not.

Consider the following property about a formal language $\mathrm{L}$ :

"There exists a number $p \geq 0$, such that for any word $w \in \mathrm{L},|w| \geq p$, there exist words $x$, $y$, and $z$, with $\mathrm{y} \neq \varepsilon$ and $|x y| \leq p$, for any integer $\mathrm{i} \geq 0$, the word $x y^{i} z \in \mathrm{L}$."

Based on the statement and your knowledge of the subject, mark T (true) or F (false) for the following statements.

( ) If $\mathrm{L}$ is accepted by a non-deterministic finite automata , then $\mathrm{L}$ satisfies the above property.

( ) If $L$ is not regular, $L$ doesn't satisfy the above property.

( ) The language $\left\{a^{n} b^{n} c^{n} \mid n \geq 0\right\}$ does not satisfy the above property.

( ) If $L$ doesn't satisfy the above property, $L$ is not regular,

Select the option that contains, from top to bottom, the correct sequence.
